body:
Rafael Mendes: Kicking off Phase 1 rollout planning for incident bot context bundles. Goal is small + safe beta next week (deploy context only) + start tracking success metrics. Linear project: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2841/incident-bot-diagnostics-improvements

Rafael Mendes: Proposed Phase 1 scope (2–4 weeks):
- Deploy collector posts “recent deploys” summary in incident threads
- Links to release pipeline + PRs + relevant dashboards
- Fail-open behavior (collector timeouts don’t block posting)

Rafael Mendes: Need owners + rollout checklist. Drive checklist draft here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rwi9Xx-rollout-checklist (WIP)

Sean Gallagher: +1. For rollout, I want us to start with #incidents only, and only for Sev0/Sev1 initially. Also needs to be obvious when bot is missing data vs “no recent deploys”.

Aisha Bello: Metrics side: I can baseline “time-to-suspect-change” + adoption. But we should be crisp on what we’re measuring in Phase 1 vs later phases.

Miles Thornton: For multi-region, deploy context has to be region-aware. We’ve had too many incidents where us-east deploys are irrelevant to eu-west pages. The summary should group by region and include “no deploys in window” per region so responders don’t assume.

Talia Benson: Can someone list the concrete owners + dates? I’ll convert this into a Phase 1 mini-plan + put in ENG-2841 as a comment.

Jacob Stein: I can take deploy collector implementation + Slack formatting for the deploy block. I’m already looking at mapping service names to release events (the naming is messy).

Rafael Mendes: Great. Tentative owners:
- Deploy collector implementation + formatting: @Jacob Stein
- Incident process guidance / responder UX: @Sean Gallagher
- Success metrics + weekly report: @Aisha Bello
- Multi-region review + edge cases: @Miles Thornton
- Program tracking / checklist + comms: @Talia Benson

Rafael Mendes: Timeline proposal:
- Thu/Fri: finalize “minimum useful deploy context” output + data sources
- Mon: ship behind feature flag + SRE-only allowlist
- Wed: expand to broader on-call rotations (still Sev0/Sev1)
- End of week: check metrics + feedback thread, decide on Phase 2 entry (config diffs)

Sean Gallagher: For the “minimum useful deploy context”, I want:
- last 2 deploys per service/region (or last 60m, whichever is smaller) — but capped
- include canary vs full rollout if we have it; otherwise explicitly say “rollout phase unknown”
- links: PR + release run + changelog

Aisha Bello: Re: metrics, for Phase 1 I’d like to track:
- % Sev0/Sev1 incidents where bot posted deploy context within 2 min of thread creation
- bot errors/timeouts rate (collector-level)
- “useful / not useful” quick feedback emoji in thread (lightweight)
- time-to-suspect-change (proxy: first message mentioning deploy/rollback, compared to baseline)

Aisha Bello: Longer term we can try MTTR deltas but it’s noisy week-to-week.

Miles Thornton: Also: if deploy context is stale due to event lag, better to say “deploy data delayed (last event received X min ago)” vs presenting a partial list that looks complete.

Jacob Stein: That’s doable. I’ll add a “data freshness” line if the release event stream lags.

Talia Benson: What’s the feature flag name? Want it on the checklist + comms.

Jacob Stein: Right now in config it’s `incident_bot.context_bundles.deploy_collector.enabled` (can rename). Also planning a per-channel allowlist.

Sean Gallagher: Please keep channel allowlist mandatory at first. I don’t want this showing up in random support threads.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Phase 1 rollout gates:
- allowlist required
- rate limit: 1 bundle per incident thread per 10 min unless manual request
- hard timeout per collector (e.g., 2s) + overall bundle budget (e.g., 4s)

Rafael Mendes: Talia can you add those gates into the Drive checklist + Linear?

Talia Benson: yep. I’ll update the checklist and add a comment to ENG-2841 with owners + timeline + rollout gates today.

Linear (bot): Talia Benson commented on ENG-2841: “Phase 1 rollout plan draft: owners, gates (allowlist, timeouts, rate limit), success metrics (bot latency/errors/adoption, time-to-suspect-change).”

Aisha Bello: For weekly reporting cadence: I can post a short update in #eng-sre every Tuesday: adoption + error rate + 2–3 “bot was useful” examples. If we want leadership visibility, I can also forward to Neha.

Sean Gallagher: Works. Also we should set expectations: deploy context is a hint, not a root-cause statement. Keep wording neutral (“recent deploys”) vs “suspected change” (save that for later once we add heuristics).

Jacob Stein: Agree. The block will be strictly factual: what deploys happened, where, when, and links.

Miles Thornton: One more thing: if there were manual rollbacks/hotfix deploys, those often don’t have clean PR links. The output should still show commit SHA + pipeline run even if PR unknown.

Jacob Stein: Got it.

Rafael Mendes: Action items:
- Jacob: draft Slack block format + confirm deploy event sources + edge cases (manual rollback)
- Aisha: define baseline measurement approach for “time-to-suspect-change” + emoji feedback convention
- Sean: responder guidance blurb for Phase 1 (how to interpret, when to ask for more)
- Miles: sanity check region grouping + wording (avoid misleading omissions)
- Talia: update Drive checklist + comment in ENG-2841

Rafael Mendes: Let’s aim to review the exact message format tomorrow in this thread.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup:

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: I’ll propose emoji feedback in #incidents as :white_check_mark: useful / :warning: missing/incorrect / :no_entry_sign: noisy.

Miles Thornton: :thumbsup:

Talia Benson: Checklist updated + linked in ENG-2841. Also added reminder: comms to #eng-oncall when allowlist opens to additional rotations.

incident-bot: (system) Reminder: for beta rollouts, use `/incident-bot status` to confirm feature flags + channel allowlist are active before paging hours.

Rafael Mendes: Nice. Closing loop: tomorrow we’ll do a quick “go/no-go” on enabling for primary SRE rotation + #incidents only.
